title: SMC Structures and FVG
summary: Market structure with BOS and CHoCH lines, the current swing range with five Fibonacci levels, and fair value gaps that turn grey once price trades into them.
description:
The study follows the market's structure as a pair of levels: a structure high and a structure low, each anchored at the bar that set it. When price breaks one of them a line is drawn along the broken level, from the bar that set it to the breaking bar, and labelled **BOS** (break of structure) when the break continues the current direction or **CHoCH** (change of character) when it reverses it. By default a break needs a close beyond the level; with the body option off a wick is enough. A break in the current direction must come after three bars that held, all later than the bar that set the level, while a break against it counts at once.

After a break down, the new structure runs from the break bar's low up to the highest swing of the last 10 bars; after a break up, from the break bar's high down to the lowest swing. The swing is the furthest back local peak (or trough) of those bars that is no older than their extreme. Between breaks a new high (in a rising or undecided structure) or a new low (in a falling or undecided one) moves the level, but with the body option on only while the level was set within the last three bars. The current structure is drawn in blue with five Fibonacci levels (0.786, 0.705, 0.618, 0.5 and 0.382 by default). A level of `v` sits `v` times the range back from the newest extreme: below the structure high after a break up, above the structure low after a break down. Each is labelled with its level and price.

A fair value gap is read across three bars: a bullish gap where the low one bar back is above the high three bars back, and a bearish gap where the high one bar back is below the low three bars back. Each gap is a box with an "FVG" label that extends to the newest bar. It turns grey once price trades into it, can shrink to the part not yet traded, and is deleted when price fills it completely.
howToRead:
Read the labels as the story of the trend: a run of BOS lines in one direction is a trend extending, and a CHoCH is the first break the other way. The two blue lines are the range price is working in now, and the Fibonacci levels inside it are the retracement zones that range offers, with 0.5 the midpoint and the higher levels closer to where the swing started.

Green and red boxes are gaps price has not yet traded back into; grey ones have been partly filled, and a gap disappears once it is filled completely. The structure is decided bar by bar from closed bars, so a level can move while it is recent, and the swing bar is chosen from only the last 10 bars, which keeps the study quick to react but makes it sensitive to noise on low timeframes.

faq.q: What is the difference between BOS and CHoCH here?
faq.a: Both mark a broken structure level. BOS is a break in the direction of the last break, so the trend continues; CHoCH is a break against it, and the first break on the chart is always a CHoCH.

faq.q: Why does a fair value gap use the bars three back and one back?
faq.a: The gap is read on the bar after the three-bar pattern completes, so the pattern's bars are one, two and three bars back. The box spans the middle bar and the bar after it, then extends to the newest bar while the gap stays open.

faq.q: What do the Fibonacci labels show?
faq.a: Each label writes the level and its price with two decimals, for example 0.618(64250.50), and sits 20 bars to the right of the newest bar. After a break up each level is measured down from the structure high, after a break down up from the structure low.

faq.q: Which alerts does the study raise?
faq.a: BOS on a bar with a break of structure, CHOCH on a change of character, and FVG has been mitigated the first time price trades into a gap.
